title: Adaptive schema-resolver and fanout for trace-enriched log ingestion
creator: Marco Nguyen
description: Replace brittle ingest path with an adaptive schema-resolver that performs lightweight heuristics to classify incoming structured and semi-structured logs, attach/canonicalize correlation IDs, and fan out normalized events to Loki + long-term ELK/Parquet sinks. This ticket implements the core runtime shim, a small registry of common schema adapters, and the trace-enrichment joiner that rehydrates span references for low-latency dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: New ingest shim can accept mixed JSON/text payloads and route 95% of production traffic through a schema-resolver without 5xx regressions
Correlation ID canonicalization normalizes at least 98% of variants (trace_id, traceId, corr, correlation_id) into x-corr-id header/event field
Fanout writes include metadata tags (tenant_id, service_name, sample_rate) and succeed to Loki and Parquet ELK sink within SLA for 99.9% of requests
Grafana latency/error dashboards reflect enriched trace joins within 60s of ingestion for sampled traces
Integration tests validate lossless ordering for single-tenant streams under synthetic load (p99 ingestion latency < 300ms)
notes: Motivation: current legacy sidecar performs ad-hoc parsing and leaves multiple correlation key formats which breaks trace joins and rollout debugging
We aim for a minimal runtime change that can be toggled per-tenant via runtime flags and rolled back quickly if backpressure is observed
This work pairs with ENG-100412 (tenant-sampling-policy) — ensure sampling metadata flows through fanout
design_decisions: Schema-resolver will be rules-first: lightweight header/field detectors + fallback to a micro-schema inference for unknown payloads to avoid CPU spikes
Prefer in-memory adapter registry with hot-reload from S3 for adapter updates instead of a fully dynamic service mesh call
Batching policy: adaptive batch size based on current ingestion QPS and recent p99 latency; initial conservative batch threshold = 64 events or 50ms flush
Correlation id canonical field = x-corr-id; we will also set x-trace-source for origin service name and preserve original header variants in metadata
Trace enrichment performed by attaching a minimal span-key and performing asynchronous lookup to span-index service; synchronous fallback allowed for high-priority debug routes
implementation_steps: 1) Add lightweight ingest-shim component in edge-proxy (go-gateway) with pluggable adapters
2) Implement adapter registry and two canonical adapters: 'json-structured' and 'kv-line-parser'
3) Implement correlation canonicalizer and header normalization with backward-compatible mapping
4) Create fanout pipeline to write to Loki (hot path) and Parquet ELK sink (cold path) with idempotent write keys
5) Add optional trace-enrichment async joiner that issues lookups to span-index and merges spans into a _trace_refs field
6) Expose per-tenant runtime flag in console and create rollout plan
7) Add integration tests and a chaos test that injects malformed events and simulates downstream throttling
8) Perform staged rollout to 10% -> 50% -> 100% tenants over 2 weeks while monitoring dashboards
rollout_plan: Stage 0: deploy ingest-shim to canary region with feature flag disabled for production traffic
Stage 1: Enable for internal test tenants + observability team; monitoring for 48h
Stage 2: 10% traffic ramp via traffic-splitter for low-risk tenants, run for 72h and evaluate metrics
Stage 3: 50% ramp and enable async trace-enrichment for sampled traffic, run for 1 week
Stage 4: Full enablement; cleanup legacy sidecar configs after 2 weeks stable
Rollback: toggle feature flag to false and drain local caches, fallback to legacy writing path
test_plan: Unit tests for adapter parsing and correlation canonicalizer (coverage > 90%)
End-to-end integration test that asserts ordering and idempotency across fanout sinks
Load test: synthetic traffic at 3x baseline QPS to validate batching and p99 ingestion latency
Chaos test: simulate Loki backpressure and verify buffer/backoff and no data loss to Parquet sink
Dashboard smoke test: verify that trace-enriched logs appear in Grafana panels within 60s
risks: Risk: micro-schema inference could increase CPU; mitigation: heuristics threshold and circuit-breaker to disable inference if CPU > 75%
Risk: fanout duplicate writes during retries; mitigation: use idempotent keys (tenant+offset+event-hash) and downstream dedupe
Risk: trace-index service latency impacts enrichment path; mitigation: async enrichment and graceful degradation where missing spans are added later
Risk: tenant-specific field variants not covered by adapters; mitigation: ship telemetry to capture new variants and iterate adapters weekly
dependencies: Infra: span-index service SLA bump and a Parquet sink throughput increase (infra-ticket INF-282)
Console: feature flag UI to toggle per-tenant (PM-450)
